title: Cross-System Constraint Monographs
record_status: Prepared content — public release not authorized
summary: Publish twelve substantial, source-bound monographs that make recurring conversion chains legible without normalizing unlike measures or manufacturing causal findings.
record_scope: Phase 197–204 definitive public-reference edition candidate layer.
publication_boundaries: This is an append-only definitive-edition layer over the existing governed corpus; it does not rewrite an upstream evidence decision, project stage, place state, receipt, or validation baseline.
Research targets, casebook classifications, outcome panels, translations, expert review, repository publication, hosting, DNS, public launch, and v1 promotion remain distinct decisions.

A source-bound context statement is not a compatible longitudinal observation. Outcome values remain null unless entity, period, measure, method, denominator, revision lineage, and receiving authority all pass a dated admission decision.

No missing artifact is treated as nonexistent; no delay, failure, reversal, cause, correction, distributional effect, affordability result, service-quality result, score, rank, or causal finding is invented.

monographs.title: Compute, power, and water
monographs.governing_question: How should readers separate announced compute capacity from accepted electric and water service and from recurring operation?

source_context.title: NERC 2025 Long-Term Reliability Assessment
source_context.text: NERC reports that assessment-area summer peak demand is forecast to rise by more than 224 GW from 2025 through 2035 and winter peak demand by about 245 GW. The assessment attributes most projected growth to data centers and distinguishes 71 GW of approved summer-capacity growth from 266 GW of prospective additions.

source_context.title: Queued Up 2026
source_context.text: Berkeley Lab identifies about 8,200 active projects representing 1,312 GW of generation and 749 GW of storage at the end of 2025. About 549 GW had a draft or executed interconnection agreement without commercial operation, and the median request-to-operation time exceeded five years for projects completed in 2025.
